history.name: Assistant

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content:
General industry guidance:
- Combo meals at fast-food chains typically bundle an entrée (food), a side (food), and a beverage (drink). They almost always include a beverage.
- Desserts are considered food, not beverages.
- Milkshakes are usually classified as beverages (drinks) despite being dessert-like in texture.
Implication: Treating "non-drink" as equivalent to "food-only" can double-count drink components embedded in combo revenue unless adjusted.

- Option A: Sum of all Non-Drink rows (IsDrink=No), i.e., total excluding Drink rows.
- Option B: Sum of clearly food categories only: Burgers + Sides + Desserts + Kids (exclude Drinks and Combos).
Then we’ll verify against any built-in summary to decide.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Caution from external best practices: When combos include beverages, a "non-drink" filter (IsDrink=No) may still include revenue that contains drink components. A correct "food-only" total usually requires allocating combo revenue between food and drink components or excluding combo lines unless an allocation is provided. Without allocation, equating "non-drink" with "food-only" can overstate food revenue.

mistake_reason: Incorrect Verification (FM-3.3): The orchestrator explicitly validated 87,604.00 as the correct "food-only" total by checking only numerical equality against the workbook’s Non-Drink figure and the sum of non-drink categories. This verification ignored semantic correctness that combos include beverages (flagged earlier by WebSurfer) and failed to cross-check whether Non-Drink equals Food-only. The applied verification criterion was flawed and guaranteed a false positive, leading to approval of an objectively incorrect result.
